output.name: Skelra — The Split Oar
output.myth: On the midsummer crossing Aun rowed the long boat with his nephew when Tavo came down off the north like a dropped sail and set his shoulder to the water. The oar that had carried them cracked along the grain. Aun wept and cursed and kept rowing with the half of it, because that is what Aun does. Ennu the Kite-Wright bound the crack with wet hide, the way you bind a split finger, and said the hide would shrink and hold better than wood. It did. So the Split Oar was hung on the Lamp Road, and still rows there, tines dipping when the sky goes quiet. South-east the Ice Hook hangs over the singing sea-ice, where Kessa went looking for a man gone through. Up the road the Net-Mouth Eel lies where Kael's torn net came up, and Kael swears it caught a splinter of this oar. Sil looks down from her drowned lamp and says the oar rows toward Aun, who is somewhere in the dark with the boat. Mind your oars in the frost, child. Hide does not forgive.
output.finding: Find the Ice Hook low in the south-east, then look a fist and a finger's width north-west of it, where the Split Oar hangs on the Lamp Road.
